newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Governor Whitman signs final welfare reforms.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Governor Whitman signs final welfare reforms.

text.p: - New Jersey Governor Christine Todd Whitman signed the final pieces of her welfare reform package into law Monday.
"The era of responsibility has begun," Whitman said.
The legislation imposes a five-year lifetime limit on receiving welfare benefits and a work requirement within two years for most parents of young children.
The plan, called Work First New Jersey, also provides for child care and continued Medicaid eligibility for a two-year transition into a paid job.
The New Jersey reforms were written to conform with federal welfare laws -- with one major exception: Legal immigrants will be eligible for state-funded programs.
